seo.title: Fess: How Well Do You Know Me? Party Game for Phones
seo.description: One player answers in secret, everyone else guesses on their own phone, and the Final Reveal shows who really knows you. For iPhone and Android.
seo.ogImageAlt: Three friends laughing together on a rooftop terrace at dusk under warm string lights, one holding a glowing phone, with dark city rooftops and a thin peach sunset beyond
seo.keywords: how well do you know me game, party game app, get to know you game, friends quiz game, game night app, question game for groups

hero.imageAlt: Three friends laughing together on a rooftop terrace at dusk under warm string lights, one holding a glowing phone, with dark city rooftops and a thin peach sunset beyond
hero.h1Sub: The party game that finds out who really knows you
hero.lede: One player answers a card in secret. Everyone else guesses on their own phone. Then the truth comes out, scores and all, and the Final Reveal shows who knows whom best. Only the host needs the app: friends can play for free using the app or can join from their browser with a QR code.

intro.h2: How well do you really know each other?
paragraphs: Fess is a party game for phones, built around one question. Each turn, one player answers a card in secret. Everyone else predicts the answer, the guesses are scored, and the reveal shows who was close and who has been guessing wrong for years.
Across the game, Fess tracks how well each player reads every other player, in both directions. You might read Sam perfectly while Sam has no idea about you. The Final Reveal puts it all on screen.

highlights.h2: Only the host needs the app
highlights.body: Start a game and a QR code appears. Friends scan it or type the 4-letter room code at playfess.com, then play in their phone's browser. No download, no account, no passing a phone around.
highlights.alt: Fess home screen: a Start a game card with New game, Join with a code and Scan a QR code, above a list of recent games

highlights.h2: Pick a deck for the room
highlights.body: The host chooses the deck in the lobby. Switch between adult decks and family decks made for kids 8 and up, and pick the one that fits the mood of the room.
highlights.alt: Choose a deck sheet with the Adults 17+ and Family 8+ switch set to Family, showing the Favorites, Make Believe and Family Lore decks

highlights.body: When your phone says "It's your turn to Fess," answer the card privately. Nobody else sees your answer until the reveal.
highlights.alt: Your-turn screen: "It's your turn to Fess" above an open-answer card asking which opinion could start an argument in this room, with an answer box

highlights.body: Everyone else sees the same card on their own phone and predicts the answer. The room shows who has locked in a guess and who everyone is waiting on.
highlights.alt: Guessing screen: a 1 to 10 scale card asking how much Sarah cares about what someone does for a living, with a Lock in guess button

highlights.body: Cards come as open answers, fill in the blank, 1 to 10 scales, multiple choice, rankings and "who here" picks, so every turn plays a little differently.
highlights.alt: Guessing a ranking: four travel habits, from clapping when the plane lands to taking both armrests, to drag into the order Mike would choose

highlights.body: The reveal shows the answer, every guess and every score, each with a short verdict. Scales and rankings score by how close you got. When the players allow it, AI judges written answers on meaning, so the right idea in different words still scores.
highlights.alt: Reveal screen: Sarah's ranking of morning, afternoon, evening and late night, with Chris's guess scoring 10 out of 10 and Mike's 8 out of 10

highlights.h2: Find out who really knows you
highlights.body: At the end, everyone sees how well each friend knows them, as a percentage. It runs both ways, and not always evenly. With 3 or more players and at least two turns each, group awards go to the Mind Meld, the Open Book, the Wild Card and the Oracle.
highlights.alt: Final Reveal: "Sarah, Mike and Jen know where you stand," with a percentage bar for each friend, the winner, and the Mind Meld and Open Book awards

world.h2: Made for a room full of friends

items.body: Choose a deck in the lobby. Adult decks run from hot takes and pet peeves to green flags, red flags and the things you don't usually say out loud. Family decks keep it light for game night with kids 8 and up.
The host sets how many turns each player gets, so everyone answers the same number of cards. Three each is a good start.
Play again in the same room and the results add up across every game that night, so the picture of who knows whom gets sharper.
Not in the same room? Share the invite link and friends join from wherever they are, each on their own phone.

items.h3: A buzz when it's your turn
items.body: With the app, your phone buzzes when it's your turn or the room is waiting on you, and short sounds mark each moment. A speaker button mutes them.
Room chat is one tap away in every game, for the commentary while everyone guesses.

faq.a: One player answers a card in secret on their phone. Everyone else predicts the answer on their own phone. Guesses are scored out of 10, the reveal shows every answer and score, and the turn passes to the next player. At the end, the Final Reveal shows who knows whom best.
2 to 10 players. The group awards in the Final Reveal need 3 or more players with at least two turns each.

faq.q: Does everyone need to download the app?
faq.a: No. Only the host needs the app, on iPhone or Android. Friends scan the game's QR code or type the 4-letter room code at playfess.com and play in their phone's browser, with no account. Players with the app also get a buzz when it's their turn.

faq.q: Can we play if we're not together?
faq.a: Yes. Share the room's invite link and friends join from wherever they are. Everyone plays on their own phone, so it works over a video call too.

faq.q: Is Fess for adults or families?
faq.a: Both. The adult decks get personal, with some grown-up themes but nothing explicit. The family decks are made for kids 8 and up. The host chooses the deck in the lobby.

Every guess scores out of 10. Multiple choice and "who here" picks score on an exact match, and scales and rankings score by how close you got. Written answers are judged on meaning by AI when the players allow it, so the right idea in different words still scores. Otherwise they're matched word by word.

faq.q: Does Fess use AI, and what does it see?
faq.a: Only to score written answers, and only with permission. Each player is asked once. If the player who answered allowed it, their answer and the guesses of players who also allowed it go to Anthropic's Claude for scoring, with no names attached. Everything else is scored by Fess itself.
Nobody, until the reveal. Your answer stays off everyone else's phone until the whole room sees it, along with every guess and score.
The host decides. Each player gets the same number of turns, and three each is a good start: with 4 players, that's 12 cards.

faq.q: Which phones does Fess work on?
faq.a: The app runs on iPhone with iOS 16.4 or later and on Android 7.0 or later. Friends who join in the browser can play on almost any phone with an up-to-date browser.

cta.h2: Who in your group really knows you?
cta.body: Get Fess on iPhone or Android, start a game, and let your friends join from their browser.
